title: Bichromatic closest pair

problem.name: Bichromatic closest pair
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Bichromatic closest pair.} Given red and blue point sets $R,B\subset\mathbb Q^d$ of total size $n$, find $(r,b)\in R\times B$ minimizing $\|r-b\|_2$. Coordinates have finite encodings and $d$ is fixed.

\textbf{Approximate bichromatic closest pair.} For red and blue point sets of total size $n$ in $\mathbb Q^d$, output a bichromatic pair whose distance is at most $(1+\xi)$ times optimum. Complexity counts coordinate-access time, with fixed $d$ and $\xi>0$.
problem.statement_text: Bichromatic closest pair. Given red and blue point sets $R,B\subset\mathbb Q^d$ of total size $n$, find $(r,b)\in R\times B$ minimizing $\|r-b\|_2$. Coordinates have finite encodings and $d$ is fixed. Approximate bichromatic closest pair. For red and blue point sets of total size $n$ in $\mathbb Q^d$, output a bichromatic pair whose distance is at most $(1+\xi)$ times optimum. Complexity counts coordinate-access time, with fixed $d$ and $\xi>0$.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Bichromatic closest pair.} $\widetilde O(n^{1-1/(2d)+\delta})$ time for every fixed $\delta>0$, by geometric quantum search.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Approximate bichromatic closest pair.} $\widetilde O(\xi^{-d}n^{2/3})$ time by the approximate geometric quantum walk.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Bichromatic closest pair.} $O(n^{2-2/(\lceil d/2\rceil+1)+\delta})$ time for every fixed $\delta>0$ by classical fixed-dimensional geometric methods; in the plane, $O(n\log n)$ suffices.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Approximate bichromatic closest pair.} $\widetilde O(n)$ time for fixed dimension and approximation factor by classical approximate nearest-neighbor or geometric decomposition methods.
